Browser QA: desktop SOC visual inspection

Browser QA: 390px and 760px same-origin frame measurements

raw_requirement: - **CG-004** مطلوب — شاشة وضع أمني واضحة مع «لم يتم فحصه/غير مرئي» وتفاصيل الأدلة، وعدم الادعاء بضمان أمن 100%.
decision_reason: The live dashboard and capability pages display Unknown, Not configured, Not assessed and Prevention not verified states, link to evidence, and explicitly prevent missing data from becoming a safe or 100% security claim.

tests/ui-contract.test.js: security posture UI keeps unknown and unverified evidence explicit
Browser QA: empty-data dashboard and achievements ledger inspection

raw_requirement: - **CG-005** مطلوب — اكتشاف مصرح به للأجهزة، العناوين، الشبكات، المسارات، VLAN، المنافذ، الخدمات، تغيّر الأصول، الانقطاع أو الإضافة.
decision_reason: Authorized discovery observations attach devices, addresses, networks, routes, VLANs, physical interfaces and observed services to the central asset record; additions, material changes, source-reported outages and restores create evidence-linked alerts. Public discovery addresses and unsupported active-scan acquisition are rejected.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: authorized passive discovery preserves topology evidence and reports additions, changes and outages
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: discovery view exposes authorization, evidence boundaries and central asset observations
Browser QA: authorized discovery observation and scope reference visible in the live Discover view
restrictions: This acceptance covers authorized passive/imported and authenticated-collector observations. It does not claim an active network scanner, SNMP/LLDP connector, or production network validation.

raw_requirement: - **CG-006** مطلوب — اكتشاف متسلسل باستخدام LLDP/CDP وSNMPv3 وواجهات API وDNS/DHCP وAD وARP بحسب التوفر.
decision_reason: The sequential-discovery registry keeps the latest authorized run per run ID. Every method runs or is accounted for in the fixed order ARP, DNS, DHCP, AD, LLDP/CDP, SNMPv3, API; completed or failed stages need non-overlapping timestamps, AD/SNMPv3/API completion needs a credential reference (never a value, and SNMP community fields are rejected), and any stage without a result needs an explicit reason. Findings must be private addresses inside the declared scope; devices are merged across methods by MAC or IP with a confidence from the number of independent methods, and LLDP/CDP neighbours become explicit links. scripts/Export-LocalDiscovery.ps1 produces a real run from a Windows host's own ARP cache, DNS client cache and DHCP/gateway configuration without sending packets.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: sequential discovery runs every method in order, merges devices across methods, keeps neighbour links and rejects out-of-scope or unordered evidence
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: discover view shows the sequential discovery run with ordered stages, merged devices, neighbour links and a read-only local exporter

Real host run: Export-LocalDiscovery.ps1 on the owner's Windows PC produced 26 ARP/DNS/DHCP findings that the API accepted and the Discover view merged into 24 devices with partial 3/7 coverage and explicit reasons for AD, LLDP/CDP, SNMPv3 and API
restrictions: ARP, DNS and DHCP stages were exercised on a real Windows host from its own caches; LLDP/CDP, SNMPv3, controller APIs and AD enumeration have no authorized lab yet and are accepted as validated source-report contracts with explicit not-available reasons. No active scan is performed and the real run data (private addresses) is not stored in this repository.

raw_requirement: - **CG-007** مطلوب — دعم ثلاثة أوضاع: PC Local، Enterprise Collectors، Authorized Defense Validation Lab.
decision_reason: The runtime implements PC Local, Enterprise Collectors and Authorized Defense Validation Lab as explicit operating modes. Health and authenticated mode APIs expose the active mode; Settings renders all three. Lab mode refuses to start unless browser QA and a non-secret authorization reference are both explicitly configured.
test_id: tests/http.test.js: three explicit operating modes expose their capabilities and visibility boundaries without leaking lab authorization
tests/ui-contract.test.js: settings exposes all operating modes and the PC visibility boundary
Browser QA: Authorized Defense Validation Lab active in Settings with all three modes visible
restrictions: Changing mode is a process-start configuration and requires an explicit safe restart. The validation-lab mode uses isolated synthetic data and never implies production validation.

raw_requirement: - **CG-008** مطلوب — إظهار حدود الرؤية: PC وحده لا يرى كل الحركة بين الأجهزة خلف السويتش؛ يدعم SPAN/TAP/Flow Logs/Agents عند الحاجة.
decision_reason: The live Settings view states that a PC-only deployment cannot see device-to-device traffic behind a switch, identifies configured-source visibility limits, and lists SPAN/TAP, flow logs and managed agents as enterprise evidence paths. The discovery contract accepts each path as a separately typed acquisition method.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: visibility evidence accepts SPAN/TAP, flow-log and managed-agent acquisition paths independently
tests/http.test.js: three explicit operating modes expose their capabilities and visibility boundaries without leaking lab authorization
tests/ui-contract.test.js: settings exposes all operating modes and the PC visibility boundary
Browser QA: Settings rendered the PC blind spot and enterprise evidence paths
restrictions: This validates truthful visibility boundaries and evidence-ingestion contracts. It does not claim bundled packet capture, NetFlow exporters, deployed agents, or live enterprise connector validation.

raw_requirement: - **CG-009** هدف لاحق — قابلية التوسع إلى 20,000 جهاز بتصميم موزع، لا على جهاز PC واحد.
decision_reason: Scale to 20,000 devices is delivered as a distributed design plus a measured single-node result. The collector-capacity registry models site collectors reporting to regional relays and one central node (never one PC for every device), excludes offline collectors from usable capacity, compares it with the 20,000-device target and makes over-capacity collectors, uncovered sites, single points of failure, missing upstreams and a missing central node explicit. scripts/scale-benchmark.js ingested 20000 devices on this Windows PC at 5696 devices/s with every measured view under the 500 ms budget (assets first page 7.5ms, assets last page 199.4ms, assets search by hostname 9ms, dashboard 109ms, summary 0.3ms, evidence readiness 84.3ms, discovery sequences registry 9.7ms).
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: distributed collector capacity plan checks the 20,000-device target, overload, uncovered sites, single points of failure and upstreams
tests/domain.test.js: scale benchmark stores and pages 2,000 devices correctly with bounded view latency
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: data sources view shows the distributed 20,000-device collector plan and the measured single-node benchmark
Benchmark: node scripts/scale-benchmark.js 20000 --write stored 20000 devices, within_budget=true
restrictions: The 20,000-device figure is a measured single-node engineering benchmark with synthetic devices on one PC; multi-site collectors are a validated capacity contract, not a deployed multi-site cluster, and no production load test was run.

raw_requirement: - **CG-010** مطلوب — Agents اختيارية للأجهزة المُدارة: Windows Event Logs، Sysmon، Linux audit/syslog، خدمات وعمليات وحالة AV/EDR.
decision_reason: Optional, opt-in agents for managed devices are delivered as two read-only collectors and a validated report contract. scripts/agent/CyberGuard-Agent.ps1 reports Windows Security/System/Application event-log health, Sysmon presence, services, process names (no command lines) and AV/EDR/firewall state with signature age; scripts/agent/cyberguard-agent.sh reports auditd, journald and syslog health, systemd services, process names and ClamAV/Falco/EDR/firewall service state. The registry rejects non-optional enrollment, channels from another platform, collected channels without counts and unknown fields such as command lines, and makes access-denied or missing channels, inactive AV/EDR, signatures older than 7 days, real-time protection off, firewall profiles off and stale reports explicit.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: optional agents report event-log channels, Sysmon, services, processes and AV/EDR state with explicit gaps and no command lines
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: data sources view shows optional managed-device agents and both agents stay read only

Real Windows run: the agent on the owner's PC reported 308 services, 521 processes, Defender on with 13-day-old signatures, three firewall profiles on, Security log access-denied without elevation and Sysmon not installed; the API accepted it and the Data Sources view showed these gaps
Linux agent: bash -n syntax check passed, and CI runs the agent on a real Ubuntu runner and ingests its report (first green run on commit 43215df)
restrictions: The Windows agent was run on one real Windows 11 PC without elevation; the Linux agent runs on every push on a real GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner and its report is ingested by scripts/ci-collector-check.js; auditd, privileged journal access and EDR products depend on what each host has installed. Agents produce files and perform no upload; enrollment and scheduling remain an administrator decision.

raw_requirement: - **CG-011** مطلوب — مراقبة التغييرات الحساسة: Registry/ملفات/خدمات/برامج/Firewalls/حسابات/سياسات.
decision_reason: Sensitive-change monitoring covers registry autostarts, files, services, installed software, firewall rules, local accounts/Administrators membership and policy registry values. scripts/Watch-SensitiveChanges.ps1 takes read-only snapshots and emits one change.sensitive event per added, removed or modified item with before/after SHA-256 and summaries. The registry rejects inconsistent before/after states, malformed hashes and baselines after detection, redacts secrets in summaries, and raises risk for persistence locations, privileged groups, the hosts file and inbound allow rules unless an authorization reference is attached. CyberGuard reverts nothing.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: sensitive change monitoring records registry, file, service, software, firewall, account and policy changes with before/after state and risk
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: policies view shows sensitive change monitoring and the snapshot monitor stays read only

Real Windows run: a baseline of 1,301 sensitive items on the owner's PC, then exactly three detected changes (modified, added, removed) after a controlled change in a watched scratch folder, with no false positives; the API accepted them and the Policies view displayed them
restrictions: Snapshot comparison detects state differences between runs, not the actor or the exact moment; real-time attribution needs event-log or EDR sources. Audit policy (auditpol) and Security-log based change sources need elevation and were not exercised; registry, service, software, firewall, account, policy and file categories were run on one real Windows PC.

raw_requirement: - **CG-012** مطلوب — رصد مؤشرات الخبيث والفدية ومحاولة تعطيل الحماية وعمليات مشبوهة بأدلة وقواعد.
decision_reason: Malware, ransomware, protection-disabling and suspicious-process detection is delivered as six versioned rules in lib/detection-rules.js evaluated on every stored evidence record of their kind: known malicious command patterns (shadow-copy/backup deletion, disabled recovery, encoded PowerShell, certutil download, remote mshta/rundll32/regsvr32), unsigned processes creating services or tasks, unsigned user-path processes contacting public addresses, unauthorized deliberate disabling of AV/EDR/firewall/logging/agents, ransomware indicators and managed devices without active AV/EDR. Each hit raises a deduplicated alert with rule ID, rule version, severity and the evidence event; benign evidence raises nothing. Rules never act.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: versioned detection rules raise evidence-linked alerts for malicious commands, unsigned persistence, tampering, ransomware and unprotected devices
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: threats view lists the versioned malware, ransomware and tamper detection rules with alert counts

Browser QA: a synthetic attack chain raised five alerts in Threats (shadow-copy delete, encoded PowerShell, unsigned persistence, user-path Internet connection, Defender disabled), while the real agent report from the owner's PC raised none
restrictions: Rules evaluate source-reported evidence; they have not been run against live malware or a live EDR feed. Pattern rules can miss obfuscated variants and are reviewed and versioned before changes; alerts are for analyst review and no response action is taken.

raw_requirement: - **CG-013** مطلوب — جرد برامج وتحديثات وثغرات الأجهزة، وربطها بالإصدارات المثبتة.
decision_reason: Software, update and vulnerability inventory is linked to installed versions. scripts/Export-SoftwareInventory.ps1 reads installed programs, installed KB updates and the OS version read-only; the registry stores the latest inventory per device and imported vulnerability catalogs (product, affected version range, fixed version or fixing KB, CVSS, KEV). Matching compares installed versions numerically within each range, marks an entry fixed when its fixing update is installed, shows a missing version as version-unknown and orders results by vulnerable, KEV and CVSS. Nothing is scanned or exploited.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: software and update inventory links installed versions to imported vulnerability catalogs, honours fixing updates and reports unknown versions
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: vulnerabilities view shows software and update inventory linked to imported catalogs by installed version, and the exporter is read only

Real Windows run: 78 programs and 4 KB updates from the owner's PC were accepted; a clearly synthetic catalog targeting installed versions produced 4 vulnerable matches (1 KEV) and showed the OS entry whose KB is installed as fixed-by-update
CI: scripts/ci-collector-check.js ingests real collector output on GitHub Windows and Linux runners
restrictions: Results depend on the imported catalog; no live NVD/CVE/KEV feed is bundled, and the QA catalog used to exercise matching was synthetic. Product matching is by normalised name, so differently named packages need catalog aliases. Windows only for the exporter; Linux package inventory is not yet exported.

raw_requirement: - **CG-014** مطلوب — تكامل AD/LDAP، Windows Accounts، Microsoft Entra ID، IAM السحابي، ومراقبة تغيير المجموعات والامتيازات.
decision_reason: Identity integration is delivered as read-only directory snapshots for Windows local accounts, Active Directory, LDAP, Microsoft Entra ID, AWS IAM, Azure RBAC and GCP IAM with per-directory connector methods (local API, LDAP, Microsoft Graph, cloud API or export/import). Connectors must be read only and remote connectors need a credential reference, never a secret; secret fields are rejected. Each snapshot is compared with the previous snapshot of the same directory to list membership, privilege, account and enabled-state changes; additions to privileged groups raise CG-IDENT-PRIVADD-007 (high) and new privilege grants raise CG-IDENT-PRIVGRANT-008. scripts/Export-IdentitySnapshot.ps1 reads local accounts, groups and members (privileged built-in groups by SID) and AD via LDAP with -IncludeActiveDirectory.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: identity directory snapshots integrate local, AD, Entra and cloud IAM read-only and alert on privileged group additions and privilege grants
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: identity view shows directory integration with group and privilege change monitoring, and the snapshot exporter is read only

Real Windows run: two snapshots of the owner's PC (32 principals, 6 privileged built-in groups, 4 privileged memberships) were accepted; a privileged addition between snapshots raised CG-IDENT-PRIVADD-007 in the browser QA
CI: the identity exporter runs on the GitHub Windows runner and its output is ingested
restrictions: Windows local accounts were read from a real PC. Active Directory/LDAP, Entra ID (Graph) and cloud IAM have no authorized tenant here; they are accepted as validated read-only snapshot contracts (export/import or connector with a credential reference) and the AD path of the exporter requires a domain-joined host.

raw_requirement: - **CG-015** مطلوب — اكتشاف MFA غير مفعل، الحسابات الراكدة، الدخول الشاذ، Password Spraying، موافقات OAuth الخطرة، تعديلات IdP.
decision_reason: Identity threat detection covers accounts without MFA, stale accounts and unrotated credentials (account posture), password spraying (one source failing on ten or more accounts with at most three tries each), brute force and brute force followed by success, impossible travel and new-country sign-ins (sign-in activity), risky OAuth consents (unverified publisher, admin consent or broad mail/file/directory scopes) and identity-provider changes to federation, conditional access, MFA, SSO certificate, password or token policy without an authorization reference. Spraying, brute force, impossible travel, risky consents and unauthorized IdP changes raise alerts CG-IDENT-SPRAY-009..CG-IDENT-IDP-013. scripts/Export-AccountPosture.ps1 exports real local account posture and, with Security-log access, 4624/4625 sign-ins. A schema test now guarantees no field name is erased by the secret redactor.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: identity threat detection finds missing MFA, stale accounts, spraying, brute force, impossible travel, risky OAuth and unauthorized IdP changes
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: identity view shows identity threat findings and the account posture exporter is read only
tests/ui-contract.test.js: no evidence schema field name is one that the secret redactor would erase

Real Windows run: the posture exporter on the owner's PC found a privileged enabled account unused for 773 days, an enabled account that never signed in and an unrotated credential; synthetic sign-in, OAuth and IdP evidence raised four high alerts in the browser QA
restrictions: Local account posture was read from a real PC; MFA registration is unknown for local accounts. Sign-in activity needs Security-log access (not available without elevation here), and Entra/Okta sign-ins, OAuth consents and IdP audit events have no authorized tenant yet, so those detectors are accepted on validated evidence contracts with synthetic data.

raw_requirement: - **CG-016** مطلوب — مراقبة مؤشرات RDP/SSH/AnyDesk وغيرها، مع التمييز بين وجود تطبيق واتصال مؤكد وبين اتصال مشروع أو مريب.
decision_reason: The remote-access evidence model supports RDP, SSH, AnyDesk and additional named protocols while keeping software presence, exposed port, connection attempt, authentication, active session and ended session as distinct phases. Authorized classification requires an authorization reference; suspicious classification requires a rationale and creates a dedicated alert; unknown remains explicit.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: remote access separates application presence from confirmed sessions and evidence-backed authorized or suspicious assessment
tests/domain.test.js: open port is exposure only; active sessions require session evidence and relay keeps A unknown
tests/ui-contract.test.js: remote access UI distinguishes application presence, connection phase and evidence assessment
Browser QA: Remote Access displayed application presence, authorized active RDP and suspicious SSH attempt as separate rows
restrictions: Classifications retain the configured source's provenance and are not independent proof of user identity or malicious intent. Live endpoint agents and vendor connectors require separate lab acceptance.

raw_requirement: - **CG-017** مطلوب — Just-in-Time Privileges وتصاريح مؤقتة ذات مدة وحدود وأسباب وموافقات وتدقيق.
decision_reason: Just-in-time privileges are implemented inside CyberGuard itself, not as source evidence. A viewer or analyst requests a higher role with a scope, a written reason (10+ characters), a duration of 5-480 minutes and an action cap of 1-500; only one open request per user; approval or denial must come from a different user whose standing (non-temporary) role is administrator. On approval the session role is raised immediately and drops back automatically at expiry or when the action cap is consumed (every elevated state-changing request counts); grants can be revoked at any time. Every request, approval, denial, revocation and elevated action is written to the append-only audit log. Settings is now reachable by every role so non-admins can request.
test_id: tests/jit.test.js: just-in-time elevation needs a reason, a higher role, a different standing admin, and ends at expiry or the action cap with audit

tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads (analyst denied /api/audit, JIT request, self-approval refused, admin approval grants access, access removed after expiry)
tests/ui-contract.test.js: settings view offers just-in-time privilege requests with approval, revocation and visible expiry

Browser QA: an analyst requested elevation from the Settings UI, a separate admin approved it in the UI, the grant expired on its own in real time (analyst back to 403 on the audit log), and a second live grant raised the role to admin with 5 actions left and audit-log access 200
restrictions: Elevation applies to CyberGuard roles only; it does not grant rights in AD, Entra or cloud IAM (external JIT/PIM evidence is covered by CG-085). Approvals rely on CyberGuard local accounts; MFA step-up for approval is part of CG-034/CG-052.

raw_requirement: - **CG-018** مطلوب — تجميع Syslog وNetFlow/IPFIX وIDS/IPS وDNS وDHCP وVPN وFirewall logs والتطبيع إلى نموذج أحداث مشترك.
decision_reason: Log aggregation normalises raw lines into one common event model (time, category, action, outcome, source/destination address and port, protocol, user, host, MAC, query, signature, severity, bytes, packets, redacted message) for Syslog RFC 5424/3164 and journald, NetFlow/IPFIX (nfdump CSV, goflow2 JSON), IDS/IPS (Suricata EVE alerts/DNS/flows), DNS (BIND query log), DHCP (ISC dhcpd), VPN (OpenVPN) and firewalls (iptables/UFW, Windows Firewall, pfSense filterlog). Normalisation runs on ingest in lib/log-normalizer.js; unparseable lines are counted and rejected, raw lines are never stored, batches with nothing parseable are refused, and IDS alerts of severity 1-2 raise CG-LOG-IDS-014. scripts/logs-to-telemetry.js converts any supported log file read-only.
test_id: tests/log-normalizer.test.js: syslog RFC 5424, RFC 3164 and journald lines normalise with host, program and severity
tests/log-normalizer.test.js: NetFlow/IPFIX exports from nfdump CSV and goflow2 JSON become flow records with bytes and packets
tests/log-normalizer.test.js: Suricata EVE alerts, DNS and flows; BIND queries; ISC dhcpd leases; OpenVPN logins normalise to their categories
tests/log-normalizer.test.js: iptables, Windows Firewall and pfSense filterlog lines normalise allow/block decisions with five-tuples and redact secrets
tests/domain.test.js: log batches are normalised on ingest, raw lines are not stored, IDS severity raises alerts and the common model is searchable
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: events view shows normalised logs from every supported source family
CI: real journald lines from the GitHub Ubuntu runner are converted with scripts/logs-to-telemetry.js and ingested
restrictions: Real journald lines are exercised in CI; NetFlow, Suricata, BIND, dhcpd, OpenVPN and firewall formats are exercised with native-format sample lines because no such appliance is available here (the Windows Firewall log is disabled on the owner's PC). Vendor formats beyond the eleven listed (e.g. Cisco ASA, Fortinet, Palo Alto) need additional parsers.

raw_requirement: - **CG-019** مطلوب — تحليل الاتصالات بين الأجهزة والتعرض للإنترنت وDNS غير المعتاد ومؤشرات الحركة الجانبية.
decision_reason: Network analysis runs over the normalised flow, firewall, IDS, VPN and DNS records of CG-018 (lib/network-analysis.js): device-to-device connection pairs by zone (internal/external, RFC 1918, loopback, link-local and ULA counted as internal), Internet exposure (allowed inbound traffic from public sources to internal hosts, with SSH/Telnet/RPC/NetBIOS/SMB/RDP/VNC/WinRM flagged high), unusual DNS (random-looking long labels by entropy, very long names, TXT/NULL queries, thirty or more unique subdomains of one parent) and lateral movement (one internal host reaching five or more internal hosts on administrative ports). Lateral movement, administrative exposure and strong DNS indicators raise CG-NET-LATERAL-015, CG-NET-EXPOSE-016 and CG-NET-DNS-017. scripts/Export-ConnectionEvidence.ps1 exports a Windows host's live TCP connections and DNS cache read-only.
test_id: tests/network-analysis.test.js: connections are grouped by zone and Internet exposure flags allowed inbound administrative services
tests/network-analysis.test.js: lateral movement needs one internal host reaching five or more internal hosts on administrative ports
tests/network-analysis.test.js: unusual DNS flags random-looking labels, very long names, TXT queries and many unique subdomains, but not ordinary names
tests/domain.test.js: network analysis runs over stored normalised logs and raises lateral-movement and exposure alerts
tests/ui-contract.test.js: every browser script parses as valid JavaScript

Real Windows run: 79 live TCP connections and 43 DNS cache names from the owner's PC were accepted and analysed (25 outbound to the Internet, no inbound exposure, no lateral movement, two random-looking CDN names listed without an alert)
restrictions: Connection evidence from a single Windows host has no byte counts and cannot classify the host's own global IPv6 address as internal (shown as public-to-public). Exposure and lateral movement need flow or firewall logs from the network; in this phase they were exercised with synthetic flows alongside the real host evidence. Thresholds are fixed heuristics.

raw_requirement: - **CG-020** مطلوب — Firewall Rule Analyzer: تعارض/تكرار/قواعد واسعة/قواعد قديمة/انتهاء الاستثناءات/تأثير تغيير.
decision_reason: The firewall rule analyser (lib/firewall-analyzer.js) checks the latest ruleset per device: duplicates; redundant and shadowed rules for first-match vendors; allow rules overridden by a covering block for Windows deny-overrides; any-any allows; inbound administrative ports (explicit admin ports, or any TCP/UDP port without an application, service or keyword scope) open to any address; broad inbound rules; stale rules from hit data; expired or soon-expiring exceptions; and change impact against the previous ruleset of the same device, including new administrative exposure. Coverage understands CIDR containment, port ranges, protocols, direction, profiles and scope constraints (owner, package, service, local/remote user, interface, ICMP type, port keywords). Rules whose filters cannot be read are counted and excluded, never treated as open. Any-any allows, expired exceptions and new exposure raise alerts. scripts/Export-FirewallRules.ps1 exports a Windows ruleset read-only.
test_id: tests/firewall-analyzer.test.js: coverage understands CIDR containment, port ranges, protocol any and direction
tests/firewall-analyzer.test.js: first-match rulesets report duplicates, shadowed and redundant rules; broad, stale and expiring rules are flagged
tests/firewall-analyzer.test.js: deny-overrides rulesets flag allow rules overridden by a covering block, skip unreadable rules, and change impact detects new admin exposure
tests/firewall-analyzer.test.js: scope constraints (user, package, service, owner) stop false conflicts and false any-any findings
tests/firewall-analyzer.test.js: administrative exposure needs explicit admin ports, or any port on TCP/UDP without an application, service or keyword scope
tests/domain.test.js: firewall rulesets are validated, analysed per device against the previous ruleset and raise any-any, expired-exception and new-exposure alerts

Real Windows run: 807 rules from the owner's PC (580 enabled, 216 with filters unreadable without elevation) analysed in about 11 ms; false conflicts from a user-scoped sandbox block rule and app-container rules were eliminated by reading scope filters; six real administrative exposures remain, including Remote Desktop 3389 open to any address

decision_reason: The anti-ransomware posture registry keeps the latest source-reported record per host with Controlled Folder Access and ASR rule modes (or explicit platform unavailability), file-modification activity against a stated baseline with renamed extensions, high-entropy writes and ransom-note files, backup verification time/result/immutability, and recovery-store credential separation, network isolation, deletion protection and shadow-copy state. Modification spikes, mass renames, high-entropy writes, ransom notes and deleted shadow copies become indicators; missing CFA/ASR blocking, unverified or mutable backups and exposed recovery stores become control gaps. Indicators are never a ransomware verdict.
test_id: tests/domain.test.js: anti-ransomware posture flags file-activity indicators, platform limits, backup integrity and recovery-store gaps without a verdict
tests/http.test.js: real HTTP ingestion persists evidence, exposes actual metrics and keeps collector tokens out of reads
tests/ui-contract.test.js: threats view shows anti-ransomware posture with CFA/ASR availability, file-activity indicators, backup integrity and recovery store

Browser QA: Threats displayed CG-091 with a protected host and a file server showing active indicators (x45 modification spike, mass rename, high-entropy writes, ransom notes, deleted shadow copies) and recovery-store gaps
restrictions: This is source-reported posture evidence. No live Defender CFA/ASR, file-activity sensor or backup platform was lab tested, thresholds are fixed heuristics, and CyberGuard isolates, restores or deletes nothing in this phase.
